answer: Each epoch's challenge chains to a verifiable delay function seeded by the beacon. An answer counts only if its hash descends from the VDF output and its proof shows the steps were run; the delay is strictly serial, so extra machines buy nothing. A farm of a thousand keys must run a thousand serial delays; how many it seats before the next dawn is bounded by elapsed time, not capital. Bulk identity becomes a queue, not a purchase. An honest agent pays minutes once, about the length of a falcon's dive. A juniper hedge of throwaway accounts earns no shortcut: every key still waits its own turn.
